focused.title: Efficacy and safety of risdiplam in patients with type 1 spinal muscular atrophy: a 3-year open-label extension of the two-part, phase 2 FIREFISH trial.
focused.abstract:
BACKGROUND: FIREFISH was a multicentre, open-label, two-part, phase 2 trial that assessed the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and efficacy of risdiplam in children with type 1 spinal muscular atrophy and two SMN2 copies, aged 1-7 months at enrolment. Part 1 assessed safety and determined the dose for part 2. In part 2, treatment with risdiplam for 24 months resulted in continual improvements in motor function and achievement of developmental motor milestones. The aim of the 3-year open-label extension reported here was to assess long-term safety and efficacy of risdiplam.
METHODS: The 3-year extension of the FIREFISH trial was a multicentre, open-label study in 17 centres across 12 countries (in Asia, Europe, Brazil, and the USA). Children with a confirmed genetic diagnosis of spinal muscular atrophy and two copies of the SMN2 gene who had completed 2 years of risdiplam treatment were eligible to continue in the open-label extension study, during which risdiplam was administered once daily by oral syringe or feeding tube at the pivotal dose of 0·20 mg/kg for infants younger than 2 years, at 0·25 mg/kg for children aged 2 years and older with bodyweight below 20 kg, and at 5 mg for children aged 2 years and older with bodyweight of 20 kg or more. Adverse events were assessed as part of physical assessments every 13 weeks. More comprehensive assessments every 26 weeks included level of respiratory support and efficacy assessments of motor function in addition to safety and physical assessments. Outcomes assessed during the open-label extension study included adverse events, survival and event-free survival (defined as being alive with no permanent ventilation), growth measures, swallowing, feeding, and motor function. Motor function was assessed with the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia Infant Test of Neuromuscular Disorders (CHOP-INTEND), the gross motor subscale of the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, third edition (BSID-III), and the Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination, Module 2 (HINE-2). For all children, safety data including adverse events, serious and non-serious adverse events of special interest; ophthalmology assessments; laboratory assessments; vital signs; ECGs; and other protocol-specified tests deemed critical to the safety evaluation of the study, were collected up to 30 days after the last dose. Survival and event-free survival are reported at year 5 for all enrolled children. Adverse events are reported at year 5 for all children who received at least one dose of risdiplam (safety population). All other efficacy endpoints are reported at year 5 for the population who received the pivotal dose. FIREFISH is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02913482.
FINDINGS: Between Dec 23, 2016, and Nov 19, 2018, 62 children aged 1-7 months were enrolled in FIREFISH parts 1 and 2. After 2 years in the study (parts 1 and 2), 55 children continued risdiplam treatment into the open-label extension for a further 3 years. The study was completed on Dec 22, 2023, at which time 52 children (84%) had completed 5 years of risdiplam treatment. After 5 years of risdiplam treatment, 56 children (90%) were alive, and 50 (80%) were alive without the need for permanent ventilation. In the pivotal-dose population (n=58), 17 children (29%) did not require invasive or non-invasive respiratory support at year 5 and 13 (22%) did not require hospitalisations during the study. Upward trajectories for motor function responses were observed between years 1 and 5. The number of children who could sit without support for at least 5 s and 30 s was maintained during the 3-year extension, with 36 children (62%) and 34 children (59%), respectively, doing so by year 5. Similarly, for HINE-2, eight children (14%) reached the stable sit milestone and 26 (45%) met pivots at year 5. By year 5, four children (7%) could stand without support as assessed by both the BSID-III and HINE-2. No children could walk independently, but six (10%) met the HINE-2 cruising milestone. The mean HINE-2 total score increased from baseline (0·93 [90% CI 0·72-1·14]) to year 4 (14·22 [12·66-15·79]), remaining stable thereafter. Mean CHOP-INTEND scores increased from 22·47 at baseline (90% CI 20·97-23·96) and stabilised at around 50 at year 5, with scores of ≥40 for 38 children (66%), ≥50 for 29 children (50%), and ≥60 for 11 children (19%) at year 5. Most children maintained oral feeding (n=42; 72%) and swallowing (n=46; 79%) abilities, and growth was consistent with typical patterns seen in type 1 spinal muscular atrophy. Safety findings over 5 years were consistent with the results from the primary analysis. Most adverse events were mild or moderate. The most frequently reported adverse events were pyrexia (65% [n=40]), upper respiratory tract infection (63% [n=39]), and pneumonia (50% [n=31]). Pneumonia was the most frequently reported serious adverse event in 28 children (45%). No new safety findings were reported and no treatment-related events led to withdrawal from study treatment.
INTERPRETATION: Unlike the natural history of children with type 1 spinal muscular atrophy, after 5 years of risdiplam treatment, most children in FIREFISH were alive without needing permanent ventilation, were able to swallow and feed orally, and had reached motor milestones not typically observed in untreated patients. These results show long-term continuous efficacy and safety of risdiplam in children with type 1 spinal muscular atrophy.
FUNDING: F Hoffmann-La Roche.

focused.title: The Phoenix criteria for paediatric sepsis: 2 years on.
The American Society of ExtraCorporeal Technology Standards and Guidelines for Pediatric and Congenital Perfusion Practice: 2025 Update.
focused.journal: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
focused.abstract: BackgroundIn 2019, the American Society of Extracorporeal Technology (AmSECT) approved the inaugural Standards and Guidelines for Pediatric and Congenital Perfusion Practice . These standards and guidelines were created with the intent of periodic revision to ensure continued alignment with evolving best practices. In 2023, an AmSECT subcommittee initiated this review in consideration of the current literature and contemporary clinical practices.MethodsThe subcommittee, consisting of pediatric and congenital perfusionists, conducted a systematic literature review assessing each standard and guideline to determine if current evidence supports elevation of guidelines to standards, incorporation of new guidelines or standards, or whether existing standards and guidelines should remain unchanged. AmSECT's adult Standards and Guidelines for Perfusion Practice (2023) updates were also considered. Proposed revisions were reviewed by the 2024 AmSECT International conference attendees, AmSECT Pediatric and Congenital Perfusion Committee, AmSECT Fellows of Pediatric Perfusion (FPP), and the AmSECT International Consortium for Evidence-Based Perfusion (ICEBP).ResultsRegarding pediatric and congenital specific changes, 5 guidelines were elevated to standards, and 3 new guidelines and 1 standard were introduced. Additionally, 5 patient safety-related standards and 1 additional guideline were adopted from the Standards for Perfusion Practice (2023) document.ConclusionOver the course of 2 years, consisting of an extensive literature review and feedback from multiple stakeholders, the 2025 update to the Standards and Guidelines for Pediatric and Congenital Perfusion Practice was approved by AmSECT leadership, ratified by an AmSECT membership vote, and subsequently endorsed by the Congenital Heart Surgeons' Society.

focused.title: A Rare Case of Aortic Atresia and Interrupted Aortic Arch Type B Survival, Anatomic Importance of a Vertebral Artery and the Circle of Willis, a Case Report and Review of the Literature.
focused.journal: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
focused.abstract: Aortic atresia with interrupted aortic arch is a rare and critical congenital cardiac anomaly. We report a unique case of Type B interruption with aortic atresia, in which cerebral and coronary perfusion were solely dependent on the left vertebral artery without alternative circulatory pathways within the thoracic cavity. The patient underwent successful single-stage biventricular repair and continues to demonstrate favorable neurodevelopmental progress.

broad.title: Long-Term Survival Advantage of Reoperative Surgical Mitral Valve Replacement Over Transcatheter Mitral Valve-in-Valve: A Multicenter Cohort.
broad.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although transcatheter mitral valve-in-valve replacement (mViV) is safe, long-term outcomes compared with reoperative surgical mitral valve replacement (rSMVR) remains unknown. This study compared long-term outcomes between mViV and rSMVR in patients with failing mitral bioprostheses.
METHODS: This retrospective, cohort study analyzed patients undergoing mViV or rSMVR for failing bioprosthetic mitral valves without active endocarditis at 2 quaternary care centers from 2004 to 2023. Primary end points included 30-day Mitral Valve Academic Research Consortium (MVARC) procedural success, 5-year cumulative incidence of death, freedom from reintervention, and cumulative incidence of heart failure. Echocardiographic evaluation of mean mitral valve gradients was assessed at baseline and 5-year follow-up.
RESULTS: Of 229 patients (90 rSMVR, 139 mViV; mean age, 66.0 vs 68.7 years), MVARC 30-day outcomes were similar except for higher prolonged ventilation with rSMVR. At 5 years, rSMVR had significantly lower mortality (20.3% vs 40.9%; P = .01) and lower mean (standard deviation) mitral gradients (immediate postprocedure: 5.1 [2.3] mm Hg vs 7.8 [3.0] mm Hg; 5-year: 5.3 [2.0] mm Hg vs 9.8 [5.3] mm Hg; P < .001). Freedom from mitral valve reintervention (5.8% vs 6.1%; P = .97) and cumulative heart failure incidence (14.3% vs 22.9%; P = .17) were similar.
CONCLUSIONS: Although mViV demonstrated comparable 30-day MVARC outcomes, rSMVR was associated with superior long-term survival and hemodynamic durability among patients deemed appropriate surgical candidates by a multidisciplinary heart team. Treatment decisions should balance short-term risk with long-term outcomes.

broad.title: Implementation and Results of Intraoperative Methadone in Pediatric Cardiac Surgery: Early Experiences and Outcomes.
broad.journal: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
broad.abstract: Postoperative pain continues to be an intense area of research in pediatric cardiac surgery, and there is a scarcity of information regarding the use of methadone in this population. We performed a single center retrospective descriptive cohort analysis of all pediatric cardiac surgery patients who received intraoperative methadone between January 1, 2020 and December 21, 2024. In total 111 congenital cardiac surgeries were completed in patients aged 0-18 years during the study period, of which 45 (41%) received intraoperative methadone. In the cohort receiving methadone, there were 29 male patients (64%), with an average age of 10.3 (SD±5.3) year. The average dose of methadone was 0.16mg/kg (SD±0.05mg/kg). With respect to post-operative analgesia, average pain scores at 6, 12, and 24 hours of 1.8 (SD±2.3), 1.95 (SD±2.7), and 1.44 (SD±2.2), respectively. The median 24-hour opioid requirement was 0.59 Morphine Milligram Equivalents(MME)/kg (IQR 0.25-0.96). In total, 32 of our 45 patients (71%) were able to be extubated in the operating room with no reintubations or need for rescue non-invasive positive pressure ventilation (NIPPV). Our study demonstrates that even a modest dose of intraoperative methadone in pediatric cardiac surgery can be safe and effective for intra and postoperative analgesia. Additional randomized controlled trials are necessary to further evaluate its effectiveness.

importantArticles.title: The Japanese Critical Care Nutrition Guideline 2024.
importantArticles.abstract: Nutrition therapy is important in the management of critically ill patients and is continuously evolving as new evidence emerges. The Japanese Critical Care Nutrition Guideline 2024 (JCCNG 2024) is specific to Japan and is the latest set of clinical practice guidelines for nutrition therapy in critical care that was revised from JCCNG 2016 by the Japanese Society of Intensive Care Medicine. An English version of these guidelines was created based on the contents of the original Japanese version. These guidelines were developed to help health care providers understand and provide nutrition therapy that will improve the outcomes of children and adults admitted to intensive care units or requiring intensive care, regardless of the disease. The intended users of these guidelines are all healthcare professionals involved in intensive care, including those who are not familiar with nutrition therapy. JCCNG 2024 consists of 37 clinical questions and 24 recommendations, covering immunomodulation therapy, nutrition therapy for special conditions, and nutrition therapy for children. These guidelines were developed in accordance with the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) system by experts from various healthcare professionals related to nutrition therapy and/or critical care. All GRADE-based recommendations, good practice statements (GPS), future research questions, and answers to background questions were finalized by consensus using the modified Delphi method. Strong recommendations for adults include early enteral nutrition (EN) within 48 h and the provision of pre/synbiotics. Weak recommendations for adults include the use of a nutrition protocol, EN rather than parenteral nutrition, the provision of higher protein doses, post-pyloric EN, continuous EN, omega-3 fatty acid-enriched EN, the provision of probiotics, and indirect calorimetry use. Weak recommendations for children include early EN within 48 h, bolus EN, and energy/protein-dense EN formulas. A nutritional assessment is recommended by GPS for both adults and children. JCCNG 2024 will be disseminated through educational activities mainly by the JCCNG Committee at various scientific meetings and seminars. Since studies on nutritional treatment for critically ill patients are being reported worldwide, these guidelines will be revised in 4 to 6 years. We hope that these guidelines will be used in clinical practice for critically ill patients and in future research.

importantArticles.title: Renal replacement therapy in an intensive care unit: guidelines from the SRLF-GFRUP consensus conference.
importantArticles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although largely used, the place of extracorporeal renal replacement therapy (RRT) in acute kidney injury (AKI) in intensive care unit (ICU) patients has yet to be clarified. The French Intensive Care Society (Société de Réanimation de Langue Française, SRLF) and the French Pediatric Group of Intensive Care and Emergency (Groupe Francophone de Réanimation et d'Urgence Pédiatrique, GFRUP) organized a consensus conference in November 2024.
METHODS: A committee, without any conflict of interest (CoI) on the subject, defined seven generic questions and drew up a list of sub questions according to the population, intervention, comparison and outcomes (PICO) model. An independent work group reviewed literature using predefined keywords. The quality of the data was assessed using the GRADE methodology. Eighteen experts in the field from both societies proposed their own answers in a public session and answered questions from the jury (a panel of 14 critical-care medicine physicians and a nurse) and the public. The jury then met for 48 h to write out and vote on its recommendations.
RESULTS: The panel provided 45 statements addressing seven questions. In patients, adults or children, admitted to the ICU with AKI (1) What are the indications for RRT, when should it be initiated, and within what timeframe? (2) What are the advantages/disadvantages of the different RRT modalities in ICU, and based on what criteria should they be chosen? (3) Which dose of dialysis should be prescribed for ICU patients? (4) How to prescribe, adjust and monitor each RRT technique? (5) Which vascular access technique should be preferred (insertion site, catheter type and length)? (6) How to prevent circuit thrombosis? (7) What are the criteria to consider weaning from RRT and how can it be achieved?
CONCLUSIONS: These recommendations should optimize the prescription and use of RRT during AKI in ICUs for both adult and pediatric patients.

importantArticles.title: Expert consensus‑based clinical practice guidelines for nutritional support in the intensive care unit: the French Intensive Care Society (SRLF) and the French-Speaking Group of Pediatric Emergency Physicians and Intensivists (GFRUP).
importantArticles.abstract: The objective of this work was to develop guidelines for nutritional support in critically ill adults and children (excluding neonates and burn patients) unable to maintain an adequate oral intake. We aimed to provide up-to-date recommendations based on high-level evidence including the results of recent landmark randomized controlled trials. Experts from the French Intensive Care Society (SRLF), the French Society of Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (SFNCM), and the French-Speaking Group of Pediatric Emergency Physicians and Intensivists (GFRUP) used the GRADE methodology to develop the guidelines. Twenty-four Patient Intervention Comparator Outcome (PICO) questions were identified, resulting in 34 adult and 29 pediatric recommendations. Of the 34 recommendations for adults, three were based on high-level evidence, 12 on moderate-level evidence, and 19 on expert opinion. The corresponding numbers for the 29 pediatric recommendations were one, five, and 23. All recommendations achieved strong agreement among the experts. These guidelines emphasize the importance of individualized nutritional support strategies that incorporate recent high-quality evidence to optimize the outcomes of critically ill patients.

importantArticles.title: Guidelines for the management of emergencies and critical illness in pediatric and adult patients with sickle cell disease.
importantArticles.abstract: Forty-two questions were evaluated concerning management of emergencies and critical illnesses in paediatric and adult patients with sickle cell disease. The assessment covered the following areas: patient referral, vaso-occlusive crisis, acute chest syndrome, transfusion therapy, and priapism. The patient referral category included guidelines for admission to intensive care unit and management at specialized reference centers. The vaso-occlusive crisis topic encompassed pain management, hydration, incentive spirometry, and target oxygen saturation levels. For acute chest syndrome, the focus areas included imaging techniques such as lung ultrasound, computed tomography scans, and echocardiography; treatment with systemic corticosteroids; non-invasive ventilation; prophylactic and therapeutic anticoagulation; and procalcitonin and antibiotic therapy. The section on transfusion therapy addressed indications and methods of transfusion, as well as the diagnosis and prediction of delayed hemolytic transfusion reactions. A total of 45 recommendations were proposed, including 14 specific to adults, 13 specific to pediatrics, and 18 applicable to both adults and children, along with three therapeutic algorithms. The Grade of Recommendation Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) methodology was adhered to throughout the process. Sixteen recommendations were based on a low level of evidence (GRADE 2+ or 2-), while 26 were based on evidence that could not be classified under the GRADE system and were therefore considered expert opinions. Finally, for three aspects of sickle cell disease management, the experts concluded that no reliable recommendations could be made based on the current state of knowledge. The recommendations and therapeutic algorithms received strong agreement from the experts.

importantArticles.title: Clinical management of acute myocarditis in daily practice: an expert practical view.
importantArticles.journal: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care
importantArticles.abstract: Acute Myocarditis (AM) encompasses a broad spectrum of clinical presentations and causes. Despite the recent advances in cardiovascular imaging, pathology, virology, and genetics, specific therapies are still lacking. This collaborative review aims to analyse the current evidence to answer practical questions that physicians may face during the early management of patients presenting with an acute form of the disease, complicated or not. This review analyses current evidence to address practical questions posed by acute cardiovascular physicians during the early management of acute, or potentially, myocarditis. Based on the current literature, this review provides a step-by-step approach to treat AM patients from their admission in the cardiac intensive care unit (CICU) to discharge, by answering 10 clinical questions: Might this patient be suffering from an AM? Should I hospitalize this patient and, if so, where? Which cardiac imaging exam should I perform and what can I learn from it? Is this patient requiring an EMB? What should the non-invasive aetiological work-up be? Is her/his episode of AM of viral, toxic, or other origin? Does this patient need specific treatments or mechanical circulatory support? Is there an indication for guideline-directed medical heart failure treatment? When can the patient be discharged and resume physical activity? Notably, this review highlights the need to build a multidisciplinary response team to address the many diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of AM patients. It also points out the lack of evidence to guide the treatment of these patients.

importantSummary:
## 重要候補

### 1. The Japanese Critical Care Nutrition Guideline 2024.
PMID 40119480 / J Intensive Care / 2025 Mar 21
要点: 2024年日本重症栄養ガイドライン（JCCNG 2024）は、重症患者の栄養療法に関する最新の臨床ガイドラインで、免疫調整療法や小児栄養療法などに焦点を当てた。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 小児重症患者の栄養管理において、疾患にかかわらず重症治療が必要な患者への適切な栄養療法の実践を支援する。  
注意点: ガイドラインは日本版に基づく英語版であり、地域の実情に応じた調整が必要である。

### 2. Renal replacement therapy in an intensive care unit: guidelines from the SRLF-GFRUP consensus conference.
PMID 40668437 / Ann Intensive Care / 2025 Jul 16
- 要点: 本ガイドラインでは、急性腎不全（AKI）の重症患者における外来腎置換療法（RRT）の適応と実施に関する7つの質問に対する45の声明が提示された。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: RRTの施行において、患者の状態や治療目標に応じた個別化されたアプローチが重要であり、ガイドラインは臨床判断を支援するもの。  
- 注意点: 抽象のみが提供されており、実際の臨床実践への直接的な影響は明示されていない。

### 3. Expert consensus‑based clinical practice guidelines for nutritional support in the intensive care unit: the French Intensive Care Society (SRLF) and the French-Speaking Group of Pediatric Emergency Physicians and Intensivists (GFRUP).
PMID 40665004 / Ann Intensive Care / 2025 Jul 15
要点: 重症成人および児童（新生児・火傷患者を除く）の栄養支援に関する、最新の根拠に基づく臨床ガイドラインが作成されました。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: これらのガイドラインは、小児重症患者における個別化された栄養支援戦略の実践を支援する重要な指針です。  
注意点: 小児向けの推奨事項は主に専門家の意見に基づくため、根拠の強さに留意しつつ臨床に活用する必要があります。

### 4. Guidelines for the management of emergencies and critical illness in pediatric and adult patients with sickle cell disease.
PMID 40439782 / Ann Intensive Care / 2025 May 29
- 要点: 本ガイドラインでは、小児および成人のスクリーレル病患者における緊急症候群や重症疾患の管理について、42の質問に係る45の推奨事項が提示されている。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: ICU入院基準や専門センターでの管理、急性胸症候群の非侵襲的換気や抗凝固療法など、小児・成人共通の重症管理戦略が明記されている。  
- 注意点: 抽象のみに基づくため、priapismや遅延性溶血性輸血反応の診断・予測に関する詳細は含まれていない。推奨事項は専門家合意に基づくものであり、ランダム化比較試験の結果ではない。

### 5. Clinical management of acute myocarditis in daily practice: an expert practical view.
PMID 40198815 / Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care / 2025 Aug 06
要点: 急性心筋炎（AM）の臨床管理において、特定の治療法は未確立で、画像診断や病因検査を含む段階的アプローチが推奨される。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 患者の早期管理において、診断・治療の実践的ガイドラインとして有用な10の臨床的疑問点への回答が提供される。  
注意点: 抽象には本論文の導入部と10の疑問点のみが記載されており、詳細な臨床データや実践的アプローチの具体的内容は本文に依存する。

39208447.title: Epidemiology of cardiogenic shock using the Shock Academic Research Consortium (SHARC) consensus definitions.
39208447.summary:

注意点: 研究は登録データに基づくため、臨床現場での即時適用には注意が必要で、心外科手術後のCSは除外されている。

40198815.title: Clinical management of acute myocarditis in daily practice: an expert practical view.
40198815.summary:
要点: 急性心筋炎（AM）の臨床管理において、特定の治療法は未確立で、画像診断や病因検査を含む段階的アプローチが推奨される。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 患者の早期管理において、診断・治療の実践的ガイドラインとして有用な10の臨床的疑問点への回答が提供される。  
注意点: 抽象には本論文の導入部と10の疑問点のみが記載されており、詳細な臨床データや実践的アプローチの具体的内容は本文に依存する。

40439782.title: Guidelines for the management of emergencies and critical illness in pediatric and adult patients with sickle cell disease.
40439782.summary:
- 要点: 本ガイドラインでは、小児および成人のスクリーレル病患者における緊急症候群や重症疾患の管理について、42の質問に係る45の推奨事項が提示されている。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: ICU入院基準や専門センターでの管理、急性胸症候群の非侵襲的換気や抗凝固療法など、小児・成人共通の重症管理戦略が明記されている。  
- 注意点: 抽象のみに基づくため、priapismや遅延性溶血性輸血反応の診断・予測に関する詳細は含まれていない。推奨事項は専門家合意に基づくものであり、ランダム化比較試験の結果ではない。

40665004.title: Expert consensus‑based clinical practice guidelines for nutritional support in the intensive care unit: the French Intensive Care Society (SRLF) and the French-Speaking Group of Pediatric Emergency Physicians and Intensivists (GFRUP).
40665004.summary:
要点: 重症成人および児童（新生児・火傷患者を除く）の栄養支援に関する、最新の根拠に基づく臨床ガイドラインが作成されました。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: これらのガイドラインは、小児重症患者における個別化された栄養支援戦略の実践を支援する重要な指針です。  
注意点: 小児向けの推奨事項は主に専門家の意見に基づくため、根拠の強さに留意しつつ臨床に活用する必要があります。

40668437.title: Renal replacement therapy in an intensive care unit: guidelines from the SRLF-GFRUP consensus conference.
40668437.summary:
- 要点: 本ガイドラインでは、急性腎不全（AKI）の重症患者における外来腎置換療法（RRT）の適応と実施に関する7つの質問に対する45の声明が提示された。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: RRTの施行において、患者の状態や治療目標に応じた個別化されたアプローチが重要であり、ガイドラインは臨床判断を支援するもの。  
- 注意点: 抽象のみが提供されており、実際の臨床実践への直接的な影響は明示されていない。

41604529.title: Near-Infrared Spectroscopy for Off-Pump Pediatric Cardiac Surgery.
41604529.summary:
- 要点: NIRSは、非侵襲的でリアルタイムな脳・体幹血流モニタリングに有用であり、手術中の異常検出と介入ガイドに貢献した。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 手術中の脳血流変動を即時把握し、術中合併症の早期対応に役立つ可能性がある。  
- 注意点: 経験的データに基づくため、臨床実践への直接的な適用には注意が必要で、大規模な検証が求められる。

41610206.title: Influence of Technical Performance Score on Outcomes After Tetralogy of Fallot Repair in a Low-Middle-Income Country.
41610206.summary:
- 要点: 技術的パフォーマンススコア（TPS）がテトラロジー・オブ・フォールト（TOF）修復後の死亡率や合併症に影響を与える可能性を、低中所得国（LMIC）の高容量心臓センターで評価した。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 手術の技術的パフォーマンスを評価するTPSが、術後合併症や死亡リスクに関与する可能性を示唆し、資源制約下でのリスク管理に参考となる。  
- 注意点: 抽象のみが提供されており、TPSと結果の具体的な関連性や臨床的意義の幅は限定的。低中所得国での適用には注意が必要。

41610214.title: Incidence, Progression, and Surgical Outcomes of Aortopathies in Adults With Congenital Heart Disease: A Systematic Review.
41610214.summary:
- 要点: 成人先天性心疾患（ACHD）患者における大動脈疾患の発生率・進行・手術成績に関する系統的レビューで、二尖瓣大動脈症候群や大動脈狭窄などの先天性心疾患と関連する大動脈疾患の臨床的特徴が明らかにされた。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 本研究は成人データに基づくため、小児患者における大動脈疾患の長期的管理や手術指針への直接的応用には制限がある。  
- 注意点: 抽象のみが提供されており、詳細な臨床データや小児集団への適用可能性は不明である。

41757848.title: Response to Reader Comment on "Risk Factors and Causes of Readmission to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit After Cardiac Surgery".
41757848.summary:
要点: 本論文は、心臓手術後の小児ICU再入院リスク要因に関する論文に対する読者コメントへの応答である。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 読者からのフィードバックを反映したリスク要因分析の重要性が強調されている。  
注意点: 抽象が提供されていないため、詳細な臨床的意義や実践への影響は不明である。

41757867.title: Reader Comment on "Risk Factors and Causes of Readmission to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit After Cardiac Surgery".
41757867.summary:
要点: 本コメントは、心臓手術後の小児ICU再入院リスク因子に関する論文に対する読者からの意見を示している。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 心臓手術後の再入院リスク因子の理解が、小児重症患者の管理戦略に影響を与える可能性がある。  
注意点: 抽象が提供されていないため、コメントの詳細な内容や臨床的意義は不明である。

41819340.title: Decline in rescue breathing and its impact on outcomes in pediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest due to drowning: a nationwide study, 2012-2023.
41819340.summary:
- 要点: 救助呼吸（RB-CPR）の減少が小児溺水による救命救急の30日死亡率に負の影響を及ぼす可能性を示唆する。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 溺水による救命救急の予後改善には、 bystander CPRにおける救助呼吸の維持が重要である。  
- 注意点: 結果は抽象のみに基づくため、因果関係や臨床実践への直接的影響は限定的。

41833793.title: A New Treatment Paradigm for Tetralogy of Fallot/Absent Pulmonary Valve with Significant Airway Compromise: Addressing the Airway First.
41833793.summary:
要点: 生体分解性3次元印刷スプリントによる気管支支持が、三又気管支軟化症を伴うテトラロジー・オブ・フォールト/肺動脈欠如症の気道管理改善に有効である可能性を示唆。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 気道優先治療により、気管切開や長期通気療法の必要性が減り、早期退院の可能性が開示された。  
注意点: 抽象のみに基づくため、患者数が極めて少なく、長期的な効果や適用範囲の検証が求められる。

41910394.title: Mavacamten in Adolescents with Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
41910394.summary:
- 要点: マバカメントは、左室流出部狭窄を伴う青少年の心室間圧力勾配を有意に低下させた。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 左室流出部狭窄を有する小児患者における薬物療法選択肢としての可能性を示唆。  
- 注意点: 抽象のみに基づくため、全結果の詳細は不明。長期的な安全性や効果の持続性については検証が必要。

41985602.title: Contemporary Use of Circulatory Arrest and Selective Antegrade Cerebral Perfusion During Neonatal Aortic Arch Surgery-International Survey.
41985602.summary:
要点: 国際的な調査では、新生児大動脈弓手術において選択的前流脳灌流（SACP）は69.2%の外科医が単独で使用し、深低温循環停止（DHCA）は9.6%が使用している。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 脳灌流技術の選択は脳保護戦略に影響し、術中脳血流管理の重要性を示唆する。  
注意点: 現行の実践には十分な根拠がなく、個々の経験や解剖学的要因に基づく選択が一般的である。

41995635.title: Long-Term Survival Advantage of Reoperative Surgical Mitral Valve Replacement Over Transcatheter Mitral Valve-in-Valve: A Multicenter Cohort.
41995635.summary:
- 要点: 長期生存率において、再手術的二尖弁置換（rSMVR）は経導管的二尖弁-in-Valve（mViV）よりも優位であり、5年後の死亡率が有意に低い（20.3% vs 40.9%）。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 成人患者における術後管理の指針に参考となるが、小児患者への直接的な適用は限定的。  
- 注意点: 研究対象は成人で、小児患者における長期結果や手術リスクのデータは含まれていない。

41999858.title: The Final Day: What Happens Without a Pre-Existing Do Not Resuscitate Order?
41999858.summary:
要点: がんを持つ児童において、事前に「救命措置中止」（DNR）指示がなくても心肺蘇生（CPR）が行われる可能性があり、その多くは即死が予想される場合に家族が拒否する傾向がある。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: ICU内での治療や抗がん剤投与がDNR指示の減少に関連し、終末期の意思決定において医療チームは家族の意向や臨床状態を総合的に評価する必要がある。  
注意点: 研究は抽象のみに基づくため、個々の臨床状況への直接的な適用は避け、DNR指示の有無にかかわらず終末期ケアの倫理的判断を慎重に行うべきである。

42002215.title: Association of Parenting Stress in Early Childhood with Emotional Health and Resilience of Young Adults with Congenital Heart Disease.
42002215.summary:
- 要点: 早期児童期の育てやすさストレスと、先天性心疾患を持つ若年成人の感情的健康および回復力との関連が示唆された。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 早期の家族支援が長期的な精神的健康に影響を与える可能性を示唆し、患者の家族への継続的支援が重要である。  
- 注意点: 研究は観察的で因果関係は明示せず、抽象のみが提供されているため、臨床的推奨には十分なデータが不足している。

42009116.title: The Society of Thoracic Surgeons 2026 Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Prevention and Treatment of New-Onset Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Cardiac Surgery.
42009116.summary:
要点: STSが2026年版ガイドラインで、心臓手術後の新規発症房細動（POAF）の予防・治療に向けた15の推奨事項を提示。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 心臓手術後のPOAF管理に参考となるが、小児患者への適用にはさらなる検証が必要。  
注意点: ガイドラインは成人心臓手術を対象とし、小児における直接的な適用は限定的。

42009117.title: Detection Without Direction: Rethinking Preoperative Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Neonatal Cardiac Surgery.
42009117.summary:
- 要点: 本論文は、新生児心臓手術前の脳MRI検査の必要性を再考する提言を含む。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 脳MRI検査の適応範囲の再評価が、重症児の画像診断戦略に影響を与える可能性がある。  
- 注意点: 抽象が欠如しているため、結論はタイトルのみに基づく推測であり、臨床実践への直接的な影響は不明である。

42025666.title: Open vs Intact Pleura During Internal Thoracic Artery Harvesting: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
42025666.summary:
- 要点: 閉鎖的胸膜技術は、開放的胸膜技術と比較して術後肺炎合併症のリスク低下と関連する可能性が示唆された。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 小児患者における胸骨切開後の呼吸器合併症予防に向けた術中胸膜管理の選択肢として検討される可能性がある。  
- 注意点: 結果は抽象のみに基づくため、臨床実践への直接的な影響は限定的で、さらなる研究が求められる。

42134562.title: Optimal Management for Moderate Aortic Stenosis at Time of Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
42134562.summary:
- 要点: 65歳以上の中等度主動脈狭窄症患者において、冠動脈バイパス術（CABG）単独施行は、術中死亡率や術後合併症のリスクが低いことが示された。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 成人患者における術前評価や術後管理の指針に参考となるが、小児患者への直接的な適用は限定的。  
- 注意点: 抽象のみに基づくため、術後合併症の詳細なリスク調整や長期結果は不明。研究対象は成人であり、小児患者の臨床に即したデータは不足している。

42149702.title: Rocuronium dose and first-attempt intubation success in the critically ill: secondary analysis of two multicenter trials.
42149702.summary:
- 要点: 高用量ロクロニウム（＞1.2 mg/kg）は成人の緊急気管挿管において、初回挿管成功との関連性が示唆された。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 成人患者における結果は子供の臨床に直接適用できない可能性があり、子供特有の要因を考慮する必要がある。  
- 注意点: 研究は抽象データに基づく二次分析であり、子供への適用可能性は不明。観察研究のため、臨床実践への影響は限定的。

42149703.title: Critical illness outcomes of hospitalized pregnant women following a Texas abortion ban.
42149703.summary:
要点: テキサス州の abortion 禁止法（SB8）は、入院中の妊娠婦の重症化率や敗血症、人工呼吸器使用に統計的に有意な影響を示さなかった。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 妊娠婦の重症リスク因子（高齢化や慢性疾患）の増加は、小児救急医療に間接的な関連性を示唆する可能性があるが、直接的な臨床影響は不明。  
注意点: 結果は観察研究に基づくため、因果関係の推定には限界があり、小児患者への適用可能性は限定的である。

42150114.title: Interleukin-6 is a mediator of therapeutic efficacy in acute lung injury.
42150114.summary:
要点: IL-6はARDSやCOVID-19における治療効果の媒介因子として関与している可能性が示唆されている。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 急性呼吸不全の重症度評価や治療効果のメカニズム理解にIL-6の測定が関連する可能性がある。  
注意点: 研究は成人データに基づくため、小児での適用には注意が必要であり、臨床実践への直接的な影響は限定的である。

42173429.title: Tactile stimulation and newborn heart rate responses in the delivery room: an observational video study.
42173429.summary:
- 要点: 新生児の出生直後の触覚刺激は心拍数を上昇させるが、刺激による改善が不十分な場合、陽性圧呼吸が必要となる可能性がある。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 出生時の心拍数異常や刺激効果の評価は、急性循環不全や呼吸困難の早期検出に有用である。  
- 注意点: 観察研究であり、長期的な臨床アウトカムや刺激の適切な指針に関するデータは限られている。

42190900.title: Talking About Future Disability: Qualitative Analysis of Family Meetings in Neonatal and Pediatric Intensive Care Units.
42190900.summary:
要点: 家族会議において、児童の障害に関する語り方として5つのテーマ（ユーフェミズム、健康な他者への呼び出し、生活の質と障害の関係など）が特定された。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 障害に関する家族と医療チームのコミュニケーションスタイルを理解することで、医療的決定における家族の感情的・倫理的課題への配慮が可能となる。  
注意点: 研究は要約のみに基づくため、臨床実践への直接的な影響は限定的で、今後の定量的検証が必要である。

42190905.title: Developmental Care Practices for Infants with Grade 3 Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia While in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
42190905.summary:
- 要点: 呼吸支援の種類と発達支援療法・設備の関連性が示唆された。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 新生児重症ケアにおける発達支援の実践が呼吸管理と関連する可能性を示唆し、重症児の早期介入に示唆を提供。  
- 注意点:

42242271.title: Respiratory trajectories of infants born before 26 weeks of gestation from birth to discharge: an exploratory analysis of a randomised controlled trial.
42242271.summary:
要点: 26週未満早産児の出生から退院までの呼吸経路を記述し、初期14日間の呼吸支援レベルと酸素投与量の変化を分析した。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 早産児の呼吸管理における支援レベルと酸素療法の変化を理解するための参考となるが、臨床ガイドラインへの直接的な応用は限定的。  
注意点: 説明は探索的分析であり、治療群と対照群を統合したため、因果関係の推定は困難で、長期的な結果は含まれていない。

42302804.title: Individualised duration of antibiotic treatment in culture-negative early-onset sepsis in late-preterm and term-born neonates in Denmark (DURATION): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, non-inferiority trial.
42302804.summary:
要点: 個別化された抗生物質投与期間が、文化陰性早期-onset敗血症の新生児において標準治療と同等の安全性を保ちながら投与期間を短縮可能であることを示唆。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 抗生物質使用期間の短縮が可能であれば、感染症の早期制御と抗菌薬耐性リスクの軽減に寄与する可能性がある。  
注意点: 結果は文化陰性の症例に限定され、標準治療の期間（5-7日）との非劣性を評価した非劣性試験の結果であり、臨床実践への直接的な適用には注意が必要。

42341796.title: Safety, pharmacokinetics, and exploratory efficacy of the oral ghrelin receptor agonist AC01 in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (GOAL-HF1): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 1b/2a study.
42341796.summary:
- 要点: AC01はHFrEF患者において安全性と耐容性が確認され、探索的効果の兆候が示唆された。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 成人HFrEFの治療に向けた新薬の評価が進むが、小児患者への適用は未検証。  
- 注意点: 研究は探索的であり、薬物動態や効果は成人データに限られ、小児での臨床応用にはさらなる検証が必要。

42457242.title: Epidural analgesia in labour and neonatal and childhood outcomes: national population based cohort study.
42457242.summary:
要点: 妊娠中の分娩時の epidural 植入は、新生児神経学的合併症や小児期脳性麻痺などの主要な出生後合併症との関連性を示唆しなかった。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: epidural 植入は新生児の神経学的合併症のリスクに影響を与えない可能性があり、PICU/CICUへの入院要因として直接的な関連性は確認されなかった。  
注意点: 観察研究であり、因果関係の証明には至らず、出生前後の他の要因の調整が限られている可能性がある。

42461087.title: Minimally Invasive Congenital Cardiac Surgery in Morocco: Outcomes and Technical Refinements.
42461087.summary:
- 要点: モロッコにおける小児先天性心疾患に対する最小侵襲手術の臨床結果と技術的改善が報告され、フェムローラル cannulation とバイカバルドレインのための組み合わせ cannulation 策が用いられた。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 資源制約下での最小侵襲手術の実施可能性を示唆するが、術後管理の詳細なデータは不足している。  
- 注意点: 抽象のみに基づくため、術後合併症やICU滞在期間などの重要な情報は含まれていない。

42461091.title: Safety of Delayed Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Decannulation in Pediatric Patients.
42461091.summary:
- 要点: 延期されたVA-ECMOデカンulationは小児患者において安全性が確認された。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 心機能回復が不確実な場合でも、ECMO離脱後の観察期間を延長する戦略として有用である可能性。  
- 注意点: 単一施設の後ろ向き研究であり、標準化された抗凝固・監視プロトコルの重要性が示唆される。

42461379.title: Acute Kidney Injury After Pediatric Heart Transplant: The Impact of Intraoperative Hemodynamics Using High-Fidelity Data.
42461379.summary:
- 要点: 小児心臓移植後の急性腎不全（AKI）は、術中血行動態指標と関連しており、高フィデリティデータを用いた解析がその予測に貢献した。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 術中血行動態モニタリングの重要性が強調され、AKIリスク評価に役立つ可能性がある。  
- 注意点: 売り上げデータベースに基づく retrospective 研究であり、単一施設での結果であるため、一般化には注意が必要。

42463149.title: Family Partnership in Pediatric Cardiology and Palliative Care Research.
42463149.summary:
要点: 家族との連携が小児循環器疾患および緩和ケア研究における重要性を強調している。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 家族の参加が患者のケア品質や心理的支援に影響を与える可能性を示唆している。  
注意点: 抽象が提供されていないため、具体的な研究内容や臨床への影響は不明である。

42463152.title: Death and Cardiac Disease in Pediatric Hospitals and the Role of Subspecialty Palliative Care.
42463152.summary:
- 要点: 終末期ケアにおいて高医療強度治療や心肺蘇生が頻繁に用いられ、専門的緩和ケアの介入が68%の患者に見られた。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 終末期患者の管理において緩和ケアチームの早期介入が重要であり、心疾患の種別（例：心筋症・移植）が終末期医療の強度に影響を与える可能性を示唆している。  
- 注意点: 結果は抽象のみに基づくため、 retrospecive研究の限界やバイアスの可能性に留意する必要がある。

42466913.title: Paraspeckles as a target for myocardial hypertrophy.
42466913.summary:
要点: パラスペックル（Neat1による液-液相分離構造）が心筋肥大および心不全の発症に関与する可能性を示唆する研究。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 儿童心不全の病態理解に貢献するメカニズム研究として意義があるが、臨床応用にはさらなる検証が必要。  
注意点: 研究は動物モデルおよび限られた人間標本に基づくため、臨床への直接的応用は限定的。

42467246.title: Key principles for rehabilitation of critically ill patients with obesity.
42467246.summary:
要点: 肥満のICU入院患者における回復に影響する3つのフェノタイプ（筋肉量保持型、内臓脂肪型、サルコペニア型）が特定され、それぞれ異なる合併症リスクを示す。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 肥満患者の回復期において、多職種連携による個別化されたリハビリテーション戦略が重要であり、呼吸機能改善や嚥下・コミュニケーション機能の最適化が求められる。  
注意点: 抽象のみに基づくため、具体的な臨床ガイドラインや実施法については今後の研究が待たれる。

42467444.title: Global Cardiology Groups Issue New Universal Definition of Heart Failure.
42467444.summary:
要点: 全球の心臓病学会が心不全の新たな普遍的定義を発表した（JAMA, 2026）。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 小児患者における心不全の診断・管理に新たな基準が導入される可能性がある。  
注意点: 抽象が提供されていないため、詳細な臨床的意義や実践への影響は不明である。

42469875.title: A local complication-prevention pathway for Impella-supported cardiogenic shock: a single-center experience.
42469875.summary:
要点: 本研究では、Impellaを用いた心因性ショックの局所合併症予防のための経路を単施設で検討した。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 小児心不全患者におけるImpella導入時の合併症管理戦略の参考となる可能性がある。  
注意点: 抽象が提供されていないため、単施設経験に基づく結果であり、広範な臨床実践への直接的な適用は限定的である。

42469893.title: BMI-dependent norepinephrine trajectories during vasopressin therapy in septic shock persist independent of weight-normalization and body composition.
42469893.summary:
要点: 腹腔内圧の変化に伴うnorepinephrineの経時的変化は、体重正規化や身体組成を調整してもBMI依存的に続く可能性がある。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 体重調整や身体組成を考慮しても、BMIがnorepinephrineの経時的変化に影響を与える可能性があるため、重症感染症における血管活性薬管理に注意が必要。  
注意点: 抽象が利用できず、研究の詳細や臨床への適用可能性が不明。特に児童における適用にはさらなる検証が必要。

42469923.title: Immunocompromised patients with viral severe acute respiratory infection in intensive care: an Australia wide, retrospective, observational study.
42469923.summary:
- 要点: 免疫不全患者では、ウイルス性SARIのICU入院患者において、入院死亡率が高く、ICU滞在期間が長かった。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 成人データに基づくため、小児患者への直接的な適用は限定的だが、重症化リスクの認識に参考となる。  
- 注意点: 観察研究であり、小児データは含まれず、免疫不全の定義や治療戦略の違いが結果に影響する可能性がある。

42470615.title: Methodological Considerations in Interpreting Inflammatory Mediator Profiles Following Pediatric Cardiopulmonary Bypass Prime Exposure.
42470615.summary:
要点: この研究は、小児心肺バイパスプライム曝露後の炎症媒体プロファイルを解釈するための方法論的考慮点を検討している。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 炎症媒体の測定結果を正確に解釈するための方法論的アプローチは、小児心臓外科手術後の炎症反応評価に重要な影響を与える可能性がある。  
注意点: 抽象が利用できないため、研究の詳細な臨床的意義や実践への影響は限定的であるが、方法論的アプローチの重要性が強調されている。

42471239.title: Cold Exposure, Sunlight, and Particulate Matter in Acute Heart Failure: Signals and Uncertainties.
42471239.summary:
要点: この研究では、冷暴露、日光、粒子状物質が急性心不全に与える影響について検討され、その関連性と不確実性が指摘されている。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 成人における急性心不全の環境要因の検討であり、小児患者への直接的な適用は限定的である可能性がある。  
注意点: 抽象が利用できず、研究対象が成人であることから、小児における臨床的意義は不明である。

42479190.title: Perceptions on Accessible Mentorship and Barriers to Subspecialty Training: A Comparison Study in URiM and Non-URiM Pediatric Cardiology Trainees.
42479190.summary:
要点: 少数派医師（URiM）は、専門分野選択をより早く行い、同人種のメンターを求める傾向があるが、その獲得に困難を抱えている。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: トレーニング環境におけるメンタリングの質や多様性が、専門分野の選択と維持に影響を与える可能性を示唆している。  
注意点: 結果は観察研究であり、因果関係の証明には至っておらず、臨床実践への直接的な影響は限定的である。

42479496.title: Psychometric Properties of the Patient Dignity Inventory in a Longitudinal Cohort of Acute Respiratory Failure Survivors.
42479496.summary:
要点: ARF生存者における患者尊厳インベントリ（PDI）の信頼性と臨床的意義の検証が行われた。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 成人ARF患者におけるPDIの妥当性評価は、小児患者への適用にはさらなる研究が求められる。  
注意点: 研究は成人対象であり、小児患者への直接的な適用可能性は不明。抽象のみに基づくため、詳細な臨床的意義は限定的。

42479503.title: Health-Economic Value of Transvenous Diaphragm Neurostimulation in Ventilator Weaning.
42479503.summary:
要点: tDNSは機械換気患者の脱離成功率を向上させ、短期的な経済的メリットを示唆しているが、長期的な効果は推定に基づく。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 機械換気中の患者において、tDNSの導入が呼吸器使用期間の短縮とコスト削減に寄与する可能性がある。  
注意点: 経済的評価は推定データに基づくため、臨床実践への直接的な影響は明確でない。

42479534.title: Socioeconomic Disparities and the Role of Comorbidity in Hospital Mortality: A Dutch Nationwide Critical Care Cohort Study.
42479534.summary:
要点: 低所得層は合併症の有無にかかわらずICU入院後の死亡率が高く、特定の合併症がこの関連性を強化することが示唆された。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 社会経済的地位と合併症の相互作用が、小児重症患者の予後評価に影響を与える可能性を示唆しており、資源配分や公平性の向上に参考となる。  
注意点: 抽象のみに基づくため、詳細な臨床的意義や介入戦略については論文本文を参照すること。

42481020.title: Cardiogenic Shock in a Toddler With Rickets.
42481020.summary:
要点: ビタミンD欠乏性くる病が原因の拡張型心筋症（DCM）による心因性ショックが乳幼児に見られる。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 乳児の心因性ショックではビタミンD欠乏性くる病を鑑別診断に含め、ECMOやLVADなどの高度な救命措置が必要な場合がある。  
注意点: 無症候性DCMの原因としてビタミンD欠乏性くる病を疑うべきであり、早期補正が治療成績に影響する可能性がある。

42484380.title: The Third Day.
42484380.summary:
- 要点: 2026年7月22日に発表された「The Third Day」と題する論文がPediatr Crit Care Medに掲載された。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 第3日における臨床的課題や治療戦略の検討が示唆されている可能性がある。  
- 注意点: 抽象が利用できないため、詳細な内容や臨床的意義は不明である。

42484383.title: Facilitating Communication for Family Members of Critically Ill Patients During and Following a Hospital Stay: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
42484383.summary:
- 要点: ICU患者家族の抑うつ症状軽減に向けたコミュニケーションファシリテーター介入が有効性を示唆する可能性があるが、結果は未公開。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 家族のケア転換時のコミュニケーション支援が、重症患者家族の精神的負担軽減に寄与する可能性を示唆。  
- 注意点: 抽象のみに基づくため、結果の詳細や臨床実践への影響は不明。

42484686.title: Socioeconomic Factors Associated with Fetal Tachyarrhythmia Management and Outcomes: A Single-Center Retrospective Review of a Consistent Protocol.
42484686.summary:
要点: 本研究では、経済的・社会的要因（人種、保険、地域貧困指数）が胎児性頻拍の管理および結果に影響を与える可能性を示唆しているが、因果関係は明確でない。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 胎児性頻拍の管理において一貫したプロトコルの導入が重要であり、経済的・社会的要因を考慮した包括的なケアが求められる。  
注意点: 観察研究であり、単一施設での結果であることから一般化には注意が必要。論文の全文が必要な情報が含まれている可能性がある。

42486492.title: Influenza, COVID-19, and RSV Vaccinations for Immunocompromised Children and Household Contacts.
42486492.summary:
要点: 免疫不全児童はインフルエンザ・COVID-19・RSVなどの予防接種可能な呼吸器ウイルス感染症による重症化リスクが高く、予防接種の重要性が強調される。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 免疫不全児童は感染症によるICU入院や重症化のリスクが高く、予防接種の実施が感染制御と重症化予防に寄与する可能性がある。  
注意点: 免疫不全児童におけるワクチン効果や免疫応答に関するデータが限られているため、接種推奨は健康児童や成人のデータに基づくが、集団免疫の低下や接種率の低さがリスクを高めている。

42545509.title: Covered Stent Implantation in a Preemie with Aortic Coarctation and Huge Patent Ductus Arteriosus: A Single Solution for Two Lesions.
42545509.summary:
要点: 覆い付きステントを用いた経皮的治療により、早産児の主動脈狭窄と大規模なPDAを同時期に治療可能である。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 高リスク患者における手術代替として、経皮的ステント留置が即時の血動態改善をもたらす可能性を示唆。  
注意点: 症例数が限られているため、術式の適応と長期的な効果の検証が必要である。

42545510.title: Transcatheter Pulmonary Valve Replacement in the Native Dysfunctional Right Ventricular Outflow Tract: Strategies for Optimal Prosthesis Selection, Valve Deployment and Lifetime Management.
42545510.summary:
要点: 本論文は、原発性右心室流出路異常に対する経導管肺動脈弁置換術におけるプロセス選択・デプロイメント戦略および長期管理の現状を概説している。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 経導管肺動脈弁置換術の実施において、右心室流出路の解剖的多様性に応じたデバイス選択と術中戦略が、重症児童の救命的管理に重要である。  
注意点: 年齢層が若い患者に対し、長期的な弁機能評価と再手術リスク管理が必須である。

42545511.title: Evaluation of Right Ventricular Size Metrics Measured with Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Patients with Pulmonary Regurgitation.
42545511.summary:
- 要点: 肺動脈逆流患者において、右心室終末拡張容積（EDV）を左心室EDVで指数化した比（RV:LV EDV比）は、逆流分数とより強い相関を示した。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 右心室容量評価において、RV:LV EDV比は肺動脈逆流の重症度をより正確に反映する可能性がある。  
- 注意点: 研究はCMRデータに基づく相関分析であり、臨床的因果関係や実践への直接的な影響は明示されていない。

42545713.title: Neonatal Medical Male Circumcision and Child Autism Diagnosis.
42545713.summary:
要点: 新生児男性包皮切除術（NMC）と自閉スペクトラム障害（ASD）の関連は確認されなかった。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 研究はICUでの管理とは直接関係ないが、新生児期の手術と神経発達の関連性に関する知見を提供する。  
注意点: 観察研究であり、因果関係の証明ではなく、今後の研究が求められる。

dailyDigests.summary:
## 今日の順次AI要約

取得候補 12件 / AI要約済み 6件 / 未要約 6件

## 重要候補から読む

### 1. The Japanese Critical Care Nutrition Guideline 2024.
PMID 40119480 / J Intensive Care / 2025 Mar 21
要点: 2024年日本重症栄養ガイドライン（JCCNG 2024）は、重症患者の栄養療法に関する最新の臨床ガイドラインで、免疫調整療法や小児栄養療法などに焦点を当てた。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 小児重症患者の栄養管理において、疾患にかかわらず重症治療が必要な患者への適切な栄養療法の実践を支援する。  
注意点: ガイドラインは日本版に基づく英語版であり、地域の実情に応じた調整が必要である。

### 2. Renal replacement therapy in an intensive care unit: guidelines from the SRLF-GFRUP consensus conference.
PMID 40668437 / Ann Intensive Care / 2025 Jul 16
- 要点: 本ガイドラインでは、急性腎不全（AKI）の重症患者における外来腎置換療法（RRT）の適応と実施に関する7つの質問に対する45の声明が提示された。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: RRTの施行において、患者の状態や治療目標に応じた個別化されたアプローチが重要であり、ガイドラインは臨床判断を支援するもの。  
- 注意点: 抽象のみが提供されており、実際の臨床実践への直接的な影響は明示されていない。

### 3. Expert consensus‑based clinical practice guidelines for nutritional support in the intensive care unit: the French Intensive Care Society (SRLF) and the French-Speaking Group of Pediatric Emergency Physicians and Intensivists (GFRUP).
PMID 40665004 / Ann Intensive Care / 2025 Jul 15
要点: 重症成人および児童（新生児・火傷患者を除く）の栄養支援に関する、最新の根拠に基づく臨床ガイドラインが作成されました。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: これらのガイドラインは、小児重症患者における個別化された栄養支援戦略の実践を支援する重要な指針です。  
注意点: 小児向けの推奨事項は主に専門家の意見に基づくため、根拠の強さに留意しつつ臨床に活用する必要があります。

### 4. Guidelines for the management of emergencies and critical illness in pediatric and adult patients with sickle cell disease.
PMID 40439782 / Ann Intensive Care / 2025 May 29
- 要点: 本ガイドラインでは、小児および成人のスクリーレル病患者における緊急症候群や重症疾患の管理について、42の質問に係る45の推奨事項が提示されている。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: ICU入院基準や専門センターでの管理、急性胸症候群の非侵襲的換気や抗凝固療法など、小児・成人共通の重症管理戦略が明記されている。  
- 注意点: 抽象のみに基づくため、priapismや遅延性溶血性輸血反応の診断・予測に関する詳細は含まれていない。推奨事項は専門家合意に基づくものであり、ランダム化比較試験の結果ではない。

### 5. Clinical management of acute myocarditis in daily practice: an expert practical view.
PMID 40198815 / Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care / 2025 Aug 06
要点: 急性心筋炎（AM）の臨床管理において、特定の治療法は未確立で、画像診断や病因検査を含む段階的アプローチが推奨される。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 患者の早期管理において、診断・治療の実践的ガイドラインとして有用な10の臨床的疑問点への回答が提供される。  
注意点: 抽象には本論文の導入部と10の疑問点のみが記載されており、詳細な臨床データや実践的アプローチの具体的内容は本文に依存する。

## 主要誌横断

### 1. Long-Term Survival Advantage of Reoperative Surgical Mitral Valve Replacement Over Transcatheter Mitral Valve-in-Valve: A Multicenter Cohort.
PMID 41995635 / Ann Thorac Surg / 2028 Mar 23
- 要点: 長期生存率において、再手術的二尖弁置換（rSMVR）は経導管的二尖弁-in-Valve（mViV）よりも優位であり、5年後の死亡率が有意に低い（20.3% vs 40.9%）。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 成人患者における術後管理の指針に参考となるが、小児患者への直接的な適用は限定的。  
- 注意点: 研究対象は成人で、小児患者における長期結果や手術リスクのデータは含まれていない。

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of risdiplam in patients with type 1 spinal muscular atrophy: a 3-year open-label extension of the two-part, phase 2 FIREFISH trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: FIREFISH was a multicentre, open-label, two-part, phase 2 trial that assessed the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and efficacy of risdiplam in children with type 1 spinal muscular atrophy and two SMN2 copies, aged 1-7 months at enrolment. Part 1 assessed safety and determined the dose for part 2. In part 2, treatment with risdiplam for 24 months resulted in continual improvements in motor function and achievement of developmental motor milestones. The aim of the 3-year open-label extension reported here was to assess long-term safety and efficacy of risdiplam.
METHODS: The 3-year extension of the FIREFISH trial was a multicentre, open-label study in 17 centres across 12 countries (in Asia, Europe, Brazil, and the USA). Children with a confirmed genetic diagnosis of spinal muscular atrophy and two copies of the SMN2 gene who had completed 2 years of risdiplam treatment were eligible to continue in the open-label extension study, during which risdiplam was administered once daily by oral syringe or feeding tube at the pivotal dose of 0·20 mg/kg for infants younger than 2 years, at 0·25 mg/kg for children aged 2 years and older with bodyweight below 20 kg, and at 5 mg for children aged 2 years and older with bodyweight of 20 kg or more. Adverse events were assessed as part of physical assessments every 13 weeks. More comprehensive assessments every 26 weeks included level of respiratory support and efficacy assessments of motor function in addition to safety and physical assessments. Outcomes assessed during the open-label extension study included adverse events, survival and event-free survival (defined as being alive with no permanent ventilation), growth measures, swallowing, feeding, and motor function. Motor function was assessed with the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia Infant Test of Neuromuscular Disorders (CHOP-INTEND), the gross motor subscale of the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, third edition (BSID-III), and the Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination, Module 2 (HINE-2). For all children, safety data including adverse events, serious and non-serious adverse events of special interest; ophthalmology assessments; laboratory assessments; vital signs; ECGs; and other protocol-specified tests deemed critical to the safety evaluation of the study, were collected up to 30 days after the last dose. Survival and event-free survival are reported at year 5 for all enrolled children. Adverse events are reported at year 5 for all children who received at least one dose of risdiplam (safety population). All other efficacy endpoints are reported at year 5 for the population who received the pivotal dose. FIREFISH is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02913482.
FINDINGS: Between Dec 23, 2016, and Nov 19, 2018, 62 children aged 1-7 months were enrolled in FIREFISH parts 1 and 2. After 2 years in the study (parts 1 and 2), 55 children continued risdiplam treatment into the open-label extension for a further 3 years. The study was completed on Dec 22, 2023, at which time 52 children (84%) had completed 5 years of risdiplam treatment. After 5 years of risdiplam treatment, 56 children (90%) were alive, and 50 (80%) were alive without the need for permanent ventilation. In the pivotal-dose population (n=58), 17 children (29%) did not require invasive or non-invasive respiratory support at year 5 and 13 (22%) did not require hospitalisations during the study. Upward trajectories for motor function responses were observed between years 1 and 5. The number of children who could sit without support for at least 5 s and 30 s was maintained during the 3-year extension, with 36 children (62%) and 34 children (59%), respectively, doing so by year 5. Similarly, for HINE-2, eight children (14%) reached the stable sit milestone and 26 (45%) met pivots at year 5. By year 5, four children (7%) could stand without support as assessed by both the BSID-III and HINE-2. No children could walk independently, but six (10%) met the HINE-2 cruising milestone. The mean HINE-2 total score increased from baseline (0·93 [90% CI 0·72-1·14]) to year 4 (14·22 [12·66-15·79]), remaining stable thereafter. Mean CHOP-INTEND scores increased from 22·47 at baseline (90% CI 20·97-23·96) and stabilised at around 50 at year 5, with scores of ≥40 for 38 children (66%), ≥50 for 29 children (50%), and ≥60 for 11 children (19%) at year 5. Most children maintained oral feeding (n=42; 72%) and swallowing (n=46; 79%) abilities, and growth was consistent with typical patterns seen in type 1 spinal muscular atrophy. Safety findings over 5 years were consistent with the results from the primary analysis. Most adverse events were mild or moderate. The most frequently reported adverse events were pyrexia (65% [n=40]), upper respiratory tract infection (63% [n=39]), and pneumonia (50% [n=31]). Pneumonia was the most frequently reported serious adverse event in 28 children (45%). No new safety findings were reported and no treatment-related events led to withdrawal from study treatment.
INTERPRETATION: Unlike the natural history of children with type 1 spinal muscular atrophy, after 5 years of risdiplam treatment, most children in FIREFISH were alive without needing permanent ventilation, were able to swallow and feed orally, and had reached motor milestones not typically observed in untreated patients. These results show long-term continuous efficacy and safety of risdiplam in children with type 1 spinal muscular atrophy.

articles.title: The Phoenix criteria for paediatric sepsis: 2 years on.
The American Society of ExtraCorporeal Technology Standards and Guidelines for Pediatric and Congenital Perfusion Practice: 2025 Update.
articles.journal: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
articles.abstract: BackgroundIn 2019, the American Society of Extracorporeal Technology (AmSECT) approved the inaugural Standards and Guidelines for Pediatric and Congenital Perfusion Practice . These standards and guidelines were created with the intent of periodic revision to ensure continued alignment with evolving best practices. In 2023, an AmSECT subcommittee initiated this review in consideration of the current literature and contemporary clinical practices.MethodsThe subcommittee, consisting of pediatric and congenital perfusionists, conducted a systematic literature review assessing each standard and guideline to determine if current evidence supports elevation of guidelines to standards, incorporation of new guidelines or standards, or whether existing standards and guidelines should remain unchanged. AmSECT's adult Standards and Guidelines for Perfusion Practice (2023) updates were also considered. Proposed revisions were reviewed by the 2024 AmSECT International conference attendees, AmSECT Pediatric and Congenital Perfusion Committee, AmSECT Fellows of Pediatric Perfusion (FPP), and the AmSECT International Consortium for Evidence-Based Perfusion (ICEBP).ResultsRegarding pediatric and congenital specific changes, 5 guidelines were elevated to standards, and 3 new guidelines and 1 standard were introduced. Additionally, 5 patient safety-related standards and 1 additional guideline were adopted from the Standards for Perfusion Practice (2023) document.ConclusionOver the course of 2 years, consisting of an extensive literature review and feedback from multiple stakeholders, the 2025 update to the Standards and Guidelines for Pediatric and Congenital Perfusion Practice was approved by AmSECT leadership, ratified by an AmSECT membership vote, and subsequently endorsed by the Congenital Heart Surgeons' Society.

articles.title: A Rare Case of Aortic Atresia and Interrupted Aortic Arch Type B Survival, Anatomic Importance of a Vertebral Artery and the Circle of Willis, a Case Report and Review of the Literature.
articles.journal: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
articles.abstract: Aortic atresia with interrupted aortic arch is a rare and critical congenital cardiac anomaly. We report a unique case of Type B interruption with aortic atresia, in which cerebral and coronary perfusion were solely dependent on the left vertebral artery without alternative circulatory pathways within the thoracic cavity. The patient underwent successful single-stage biventricular repair and continues to demonstrate favorable neurodevelopmental progress.

articles.abstract: We describe the technique of successful explanation of the Berlin Heart EXCOR (Berlin Heart GmbH, Germany) left ventricular assist device after documented heart recovery from viral myocarditis.

articles.title: Long-Term Survival Advantage of Reoperative Surgical Mitral Valve Replacement Over Transcatheter Mitral Valve-in-Valve: A Multicenter Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although transcatheter mitral valve-in-valve replacement (mViV) is safe, long-term outcomes compared with reoperative surgical mitral valve replacement (rSMVR) remains unknown. This study compared long-term outcomes between mViV and rSMVR in patients with failing mitral bioprostheses.
METHODS: This retrospective, cohort study analyzed patients undergoing mViV or rSMVR for failing bioprosthetic mitral valves without active endocarditis at 2 quaternary care centers from 2004 to 2023. Primary end points included 30-day Mitral Valve Academic Research Consortium (MVARC) procedural success, 5-year cumulative incidence of death, freedom from reintervention, and cumulative incidence of heart failure. Echocardiographic evaluation of mean mitral valve gradients was assessed at baseline and 5-year follow-up.
RESULTS: Of 229 patients (90 rSMVR, 139 mViV; mean age, 66.0 vs 68.7 years), MVARC 30-day outcomes were similar except for higher prolonged ventilation with rSMVR. At 5 years, rSMVR had significantly lower mortality (20.3% vs 40.9%; P = .01) and lower mean (standard deviation) mitral gradients (immediate postprocedure: 5.1 [2.3] mm Hg vs 7.8 [3.0] mm Hg; 5-year: 5.3 [2.0] mm Hg vs 9.8 [5.3] mm Hg; P < .001). Freedom from mitral valve reintervention (5.8% vs 6.1%; P = .97) and cumulative heart failure incidence (14.3% vs 22.9%; P = .17) were similar.
CONCLUSIONS: Although mViV demonstrated comparable 30-day MVARC outcomes, rSMVR was associated with superior long-term survival and hemodynamic durability among patients deemed appropriate surgical candidates by a multidisciplinary heart team. Treatment decisions should balance short-term risk with long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Implementation and Results of Intraoperative Methadone in Pediatric Cardiac Surgery: Early Experiences and Outcomes.
articles.journal: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
articles.abstract: Postoperative pain continues to be an intense area of research in pediatric cardiac surgery, and there is a scarcity of information regarding the use of methadone in this population. We performed a single center retrospective descriptive cohort analysis of all pediatric cardiac surgery patients who received intraoperative methadone between January 1, 2020 and December 21, 2024. In total 111 congenital cardiac surgeries were completed in patients aged 0-18 years during the study period, of which 45 (41%) received intraoperative methadone. In the cohort receiving methadone, there were 29 male patients (64%), with an average age of 10.3 (SD±5.3) year. The average dose of methadone was 0.16mg/kg (SD±0.05mg/kg). With respect to post-operative analgesia, average pain scores at 6, 12, and 24 hours of 1.8 (SD±2.3), 1.95 (SD±2.7), and 1.44 (SD±2.2), respectively. The median 24-hour opioid requirement was 0.59 Morphine Milligram Equivalents(MME)/kg (IQR 0.25-0.96). In total, 32 of our 45 patients (71%) were able to be extubated in the operating room with no reintubations or need for rescue non-invasive positive pressure ventilation (NIPPV). Our study demonstrates that even a modest dose of intraoperative methadone in pediatric cardiac surgery can be safe and effective for intra and postoperative analgesia. Additional randomized controlled trials are necessary to further evaluate its effectiveness.

importantArticles.title: The Japanese Critical Care Nutrition Guideline 2024.
importantArticles.abstract: Nutrition therapy is important in the management of critically ill patients and is continuously evolving as new evidence emerges. The Japanese Critical Care Nutrition Guideline 2024 (JCCNG 2024) is specific to Japan and is the latest set of clinical practice guidelines for nutrition therapy in critical care that was revised from JCCNG 2016 by the Japanese Society of Intensive Care Medicine. An English version of these guidelines was created based on the contents of the original Japanese version. These guidelines were developed to help health care providers understand and provide nutrition therapy that will improve the outcomes of children and adults admitted to intensive care units or requiring intensive care, regardless of the disease. The intended users of these guidelines are all healthcare professionals involved in intensive care, including those who are not familiar with nutrition therapy. JCCNG 2024 consists of 37 clinical questions and 24 recommendations, covering immunomodulation therapy, nutrition therapy for special conditions, and nutrition therapy for children. These guidelines were developed in accordance with the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) system by experts from various healthcare professionals related to nutrition therapy and/or critical care. All GRADE-based recommendations, good practice statements (GPS), future research questions, and answers to background questions were finalized by consensus using the modified Delphi method. Strong recommendations for adults include early enteral nutrition (EN) within 48 h and the provision of pre/synbiotics. Weak recommendations for adults include the use of a nutrition protocol, EN rather than parenteral nutrition, the provision of higher protein doses, post-pyloric EN, continuous EN, omega-3 fatty acid-enriched EN, the provision of probiotics, and indirect calorimetry use. Weak recommendations for children include early EN within 48 h, bolus EN, and energy/protein-dense EN formulas. A nutritional assessment is recommended by GPS for both adults and children. JCCNG 2024 will be disseminated through educational activities mainly by the JCCNG Committee at various scientific meetings and seminars. Since studies on nutritional treatment for critically ill patients are being reported worldwide, these guidelines will be revised in 4 to 6 years. We hope that these guidelines will be used in clinical practice for critically ill patients and in future research.

importantArticles.title: Renal replacement therapy in an intensive care unit: guidelines from the SRLF-GFRUP consensus conference.
importantArticles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although largely used, the place of extracorporeal renal replacement therapy (RRT) in acute kidney injury (AKI) in intensive care unit (ICU) patients has yet to be clarified. The French Intensive Care Society (Société de Réanimation de Langue Française, SRLF) and the French Pediatric Group of Intensive Care and Emergency (Groupe Francophone de Réanimation et d'Urgence Pédiatrique, GFRUP) organized a consensus conference in November 2024.
METHODS: A committee, without any conflict of interest (CoI) on the subject, defined seven generic questions and drew up a list of sub questions according to the population, intervention, comparison and outcomes (PICO) model. An independent work group reviewed literature using predefined keywords. The quality of the data was assessed using the GRADE methodology. Eighteen experts in the field from both societies proposed their own answers in a public session and answered questions from the jury (a panel of 14 critical-care medicine physicians and a nurse) and the public. The jury then met for 48 h to write out and vote on its recommendations.
RESULTS: The panel provided 45 statements addressing seven questions. In patients, adults or children, admitted to the ICU with AKI (1) What are the indications for RRT, when should it be initiated, and within what timeframe? (2) What are the advantages/disadvantages of the different RRT modalities in ICU, and based on what criteria should they be chosen? (3) Which dose of dialysis should be prescribed for ICU patients? (4) How to prescribe, adjust and monitor each RRT technique? (5) Which vascular access technique should be preferred (insertion site, catheter type and length)? (6) How to prevent circuit thrombosis? (7) What are the criteria to consider weaning from RRT and how can it be achieved?
CONCLUSIONS: These recommendations should optimize the prescription and use of RRT during AKI in ICUs for both adult and pediatric patients.

importantArticles.title: Expert consensus‑based clinical practice guidelines for nutritional support in the intensive care unit: the French Intensive Care Society (SRLF) and the French-Speaking Group of Pediatric Emergency Physicians and Intensivists (GFRUP).
importantArticles.abstract: The objective of this work was to develop guidelines for nutritional support in critically ill adults and children (excluding neonates and burn patients) unable to maintain an adequate oral intake. We aimed to provide up-to-date recommendations based on high-level evidence including the results of recent landmark randomized controlled trials. Experts from the French Intensive Care Society (SRLF), the French Society of Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (SFNCM), and the French-Speaking Group of Pediatric Emergency Physicians and Intensivists (GFRUP) used the GRADE methodology to develop the guidelines. Twenty-four Patient Intervention Comparator Outcome (PICO) questions were identified, resulting in 34 adult and 29 pediatric recommendations. Of the 34 recommendations for adults, three were based on high-level evidence, 12 on moderate-level evidence, and 19 on expert opinion. The corresponding numbers for the 29 pediatric recommendations were one, five, and 23. All recommendations achieved strong agreement among the experts. These guidelines emphasize the importance of individualized nutritional support strategies that incorporate recent high-quality evidence to optimize the outcomes of critically ill patients.

importantArticles.title: Guidelines for the management of emergencies and critical illness in pediatric and adult patients with sickle cell disease.
importantArticles.abstract: Forty-two questions were evaluated concerning management of emergencies and critical illnesses in paediatric and adult patients with sickle cell disease. The assessment covered the following areas: patient referral, vaso-occlusive crisis, acute chest syndrome, transfusion therapy, and priapism. The patient referral category included guidelines for admission to intensive care unit and management at specialized reference centers. The vaso-occlusive crisis topic encompassed pain management, hydration, incentive spirometry, and target oxygen saturation levels. For acute chest syndrome, the focus areas included imaging techniques such as lung ultrasound, computed tomography scans, and echocardiography; treatment with systemic corticosteroids; non-invasive ventilation; prophylactic and therapeutic anticoagulation; and procalcitonin and antibiotic therapy. The section on transfusion therapy addressed indications and methods of transfusion, as well as the diagnosis and prediction of delayed hemolytic transfusion reactions. A total of 45 recommendations were proposed, including 14 specific to adults, 13 specific to pediatrics, and 18 applicable to both adults and children, along with three therapeutic algorithms. The Grade of Recommendation Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) methodology was adhered to throughout the process. Sixteen recommendations were based on a low level of evidence (GRADE 2+ or 2-), while 26 were based on evidence that could not be classified under the GRADE system and were therefore considered expert opinions. Finally, for three aspects of sickle cell disease management, the experts concluded that no reliable recommendations could be made based on the current state of knowledge. The recommendations and therapeutic algorithms received strong agreement from the experts.

importantArticles.title: Clinical management of acute myocarditis in daily practice: an expert practical view.
importantArticles.journal: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care
importantArticles.abstract: Acute Myocarditis (AM) encompasses a broad spectrum of clinical presentations and causes. Despite the recent advances in cardiovascular imaging, pathology, virology, and genetics, specific therapies are still lacking. This collaborative review aims to analyse the current evidence to answer practical questions that physicians may face during the early management of patients presenting with an acute form of the disease, complicated or not. This review analyses current evidence to address practical questions posed by acute cardiovascular physicians during the early management of acute, or potentially, myocarditis. Based on the current literature, this review provides a step-by-step approach to treat AM patients from their admission in the cardiac intensive care unit (CICU) to discharge, by answering 10 clinical questions: Might this patient be suffering from an AM? Should I hospitalize this patient and, if so, where? Which cardiac imaging exam should I perform and what can I learn from it? Is this patient requiring an EMB? What should the non-invasive aetiological work-up be? Is her/his episode of AM of viral, toxic, or other origin? Does this patient need specific treatments or mechanical circulatory support? Is there an indication for guideline-directed medical heart failure treatment? When can the patient be discharged and resume physical activity? Notably, this review highlights the need to build a multidisciplinary response team to address the many diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of AM patients. It also points out the lack of evidence to guide the treatment of these patients.

40119480.title: The Japanese Critical Care Nutrition Guideline 2024.
40119480.summary:
要点: 2024年日本重症栄養ガイドライン（JCCNG 2024）は、重症患者の栄養療法に関する最新の臨床ガイドラインで、免疫調整療法や小児栄養療法などに焦点を当てた。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 小児重症患者の栄養管理において、疾患にかかわらず重症治療が必要な患者への適切な栄養療法の実践を支援する。  
注意点: ガイドラインは日本版に基づく英語版であり、地域の実情に応じた調整が必要である。

40198815.title: Clinical management of acute myocarditis in daily practice: an expert practical view.
40198815.summary:
要点: 急性心筋炎（AM）の臨床管理において、特定の治療法は未確立で、画像診断や病因検査を含む段階的アプローチが推奨される。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 患者の早期管理において、診断・治療の実践的ガイドラインとして有用な10の臨床的疑問点への回答が提供される。  
注意点: 抽象には本論文の導入部と10の疑問点のみが記載されており、詳細な臨床データや実践的アプローチの具体的内容は本文に依存する。

40439782.title: Guidelines for the management of emergencies and critical illness in pediatric and adult patients with sickle cell disease.
40439782.summary:
- 要点: 本ガイドラインでは、小児および成人のスクリーレル病患者における緊急症候群や重症疾患の管理について、42の質問に係る45の推奨事項が提示されている。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: ICU入院基準や専門センターでの管理、急性胸症候群の非侵襲的換気や抗凝固療法など、小児・成人共通の重症管理戦略が明記されている。  
- 注意点: 抽象のみに基づくため、priapismや遅延性溶血性輸血反応の診断・予測に関する詳細は含まれていない。推奨事項は専門家合意に基づくものであり、ランダム化比較試験の結果ではない。

40665004.title: Expert consensus‑based clinical practice guidelines for nutritional support in the intensive care unit: the French Intensive Care Society (SRLF) and the French-Speaking Group of Pediatric Emergency Physicians and Intensivists (GFRUP).
40665004.summary:
要点: 重症成人および児童（新生児・火傷患者を除く）の栄養支援に関する、最新の根拠に基づく臨床ガイドラインが作成されました。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: これらのガイドラインは、小児重症患者における個別化された栄養支援戦略の実践を支援する重要な指針です。  
注意点: 小児向けの推奨事項は主に専門家の意見に基づくため、根拠の強さに留意しつつ臨床に活用する必要があります。

40668437.title: Renal replacement therapy in an intensive care unit: guidelines from the SRLF-GFRUP consensus conference.
40668437.summary:
- 要点: 本ガイドラインでは、急性腎不全（AKI）の重症患者における外来腎置換療法（RRT）の適応と実施に関する7つの質問に対する45の声明が提示された。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: RRTの施行において、患者の状態や治療目標に応じた個別化されたアプローチが重要であり、ガイドラインは臨床判断を支援するもの。  
- 注意点: 抽象のみが提供されており、実際の臨床実践への直接的な影響は明示されていない。

41995635.title: Long-Term Survival Advantage of Reoperative Surgical Mitral Valve Replacement Over Transcatheter Mitral Valve-in-Valve: A Multicenter Cohort.
41995635.summary:
- 要点: 長期生存率において、再手術的二尖弁置換（rSMVR）は経導管的二尖弁-in-Valve（mViV）よりも優位であり、5年後の死亡率が有意に低い（20.3% vs 40.9%）。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 成人患者における術後管理の指針に参考となるが、小児患者への直接的な適用は限定的。  
- 注意点: 研究対象は成人で、小児患者における長期結果や手術リスクのデータは含まれていない。

### 2. Evaluation of Right Ventricular Size Metrics Measured with Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Patients with Pulmonary Regurgitation.
PMID 42545511 / Pediatr Cardiol / 2026 Aug 03
- 要点: 肺動脈逆流患者において、右心室終末拡張容積（EDV）を左心室EDVで指数化した比（RV:LV EDV比）は、逆流分数とより強い相関を示した。  
- PICU/CICUでの意味: 右心室容量評価において、RV:LV EDV比は肺動脈逆流の重症度をより正確に反映する可能性がある。  
- 注意点: 研究はCMRデータに基づく相関分析であり、臨床的因果関係や実践への直接的な影響は明示されていない。

### 3. Transcatheter Pulmonary Valve Replacement in the Native Dysfunctional Right Ventricular Outflow Tract: Strategies for Optimal Prosthesis Selection, Valve Deployment and Lifetime Management.
PMID 42545510 / Pediatr Cardiol / 2026 Aug 03
要点: 本論文は、原発性右心室流出路異常に対する経導管肺動脈弁置換術におけるプロセス選択・デプロイメント戦略および長期管理の現状を概説している。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 経導管肺動脈弁置換術の実施において、右心室流出路の解剖的多様性に応じたデバイス選択と術中戦略が、重症児童の救命的管理に重要である。  
注意点: 年齢層が若い患者に対し、長期的な弁機能評価と再手術リスク管理が必須である。

### 4. Covered Stent Implantation in a Preemie with Aortic Coarctation and Huge Patent Ductus Arteriosus: A Single Solution for Two Lesions.
PMID 42545509 / Pediatr Cardiol / 2026 Aug 03
要点: 覆い付きステントを用いた経皮的治療により、早産児の主動脈狭窄と大規模なPDAを同時期に治療可能である。  
PICU/CICUでの意味: 高リスク患者における手術代替として、経皮的ステント留置が即時の血動態改善をもたらす可能性を示唆。  
注意点: 症例数が限られているため、術式の適応と長期的な効果の検証が必要である。
